title: Reality in Advertising (Rosser Reeves, 1961)
supports: Bibliographic record of Reeves's book (Knopf, 1961), a summary of what makes advertising succeed; source of the unique selling proposition idea summarised in the canon

title: Ogilvy on Advertising (David Ogilvy)
supports: Ogilvy's practical guide (Vintage paperback, March 1985) covering effective ads, persuasive copy and research

title: A Technique for Producing Ideas (James Webb Young)
supports: Bibliographic record of Young's book, first published by Advertising Publications, Inc. (listed as 1940, with a 1944 edition note), later NTC Business Books

title: Hey, Whipple, Squeeze This: a guide to creating great ads (Luke Sullivan)
supports: Bibliographic record of Sullivan's book, first published by John Wiley in 1998, with six editions listed

title: Books (How Brands Grow; Building Distinctive Brand Assets)
supports: Jenni Romaniuk, Building Distinctive Brand Assets (Oxford University Press, March 2018), covering celebrities, taglines, jingles and advertising as brand cues; Byron Sharp, How Brands Grow (OUP, 2010)

title: FTC Policy Statement on Deception (14 October 1983)
supports: Three elements of deception; net impression; accurate body text may not cure a false headline because consumers may only glance at the headline; fine print and disclaimers may not cure; puffery and opinion

title: Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business (April 2001, edited January 2025)
supports: Truthful, non-deceptive ads with a reasonable basis before they run; express and implied claims; clear and conspicuous disclosures near the claim; free offers; truthful comparisons; Made in USA; bait advertising

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Endorsements reflect honest experience; a TV host's paid positive opinion is an endorsement to disclose; an audible endorsement needs at least an audible disclosure; results read as typical; customers who expect a benefit for comments must be disclosed

title: 47 CFR 73.1212, Sponsorship identification; list retention; related requirements
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (reproduction of the eCFR text)
supports: The official eCFR page redirects automated fetches to a bot check, so the LII reproduction was used. Stations must announce paid matter and who paid; for commercial products, naming the sponsor or product is enough; 2024 foreign governmental entity disclosure

title: The CAP Code (UK Code of Non-broadcast Advertising and Direct & Promotional Marketing)
supports: Scope (non-broadcast ads, sales promotions, direct marketing) and section list, including recognition of marketing communications, misleading advertising, privacy, environmental claims and use of data for marketing

title: The BCAP Code (UK Code of Broadcast Advertising)
supports: Rules for radio and TV ads on Ofcom-licensed services, enforced by the ASA; section list including misleading advertising, environmental claims and radio categories needing central copy clearance

title: Bespoke copy advice
supports: Pre-publication advice on non-broadcast ads against the CAP Code; standard enquiry free with a 3 to 5 working day response; advice not binding; TV ads go to Clearcast and radio ads to Radiocentre

title: Clearance
supports: Radiocentre clears commercial radio ads against the BCAP Code; special category ads (gambling, alcohol, finance, health and beauty, slimming, environmental claims and others) must be pre-cleared; target of 24 hours in office hours

title: Unfair commercial practices (CMA207; published 4 April 2025, updated 18 November 2025)
supports: CMA guidance on the business-to-consumer practices prohibited under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, with examples and a price transparency update

title: Green Claims Code: environmental claims on goods and services (20 September 2021)
supports: Six principles for environmental claims; broad terms such as green, sustainable or eco-friendly are likely to mislead unless the business can prove them; comparisons must be fair and like for like

title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
supports: Directive 2005/29/EC covers unfair B2C practices; 2019/2161 amendments apply from 28 May 2022; Directive 2024/825 applies from 27 September 2026; 2021 guidance notice; Directive 2006/114/EC comparative advertising rules

title: Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition (Directive (EU) 2024/825): Questions and Answers (September 2026)
publisher: European Commission, DG Justice and Consumers
supports: Generic environmental claims (eco-friendly, green, climate friendly and similar) banned without recognised excellent environmental performance; specifics must be on the same medium; offset-based neutrality claims banned; if there is no space to specify a claim on a poster or billboard, do not make it

title: RAB Guide to Writing Great Radio Copy
supports: A 10-step method: client needs questions, positioning, commercial styles, one idea per spot, write for the ear, read aloud and time it, the opening line is the headline, avoid cliches, copyrighted music needs rights

title: Creativity (how to make radio ads)
supports: Know the spot length including legal copy; single-minded messages; consistent voice and audio cues; music options (commercial tracks, library, bespoke); briefing; record the legal voiceover first

title: Seven Deadly Sins of Radio Advertising (Clare Milner, 19 July 2017)
supports: Avoid reading out long phone numbers and web addresses, DJ spoofs, 'now on', lazy famous voices, joke legals, 'this is the sound of', and repeating the brand name in scripted conversation

title: The effect of lengthy terms and conditions on consumer attention and perceptions (November 2013)
publisher: Radio Advertising Bureau (UK), hosted by Radiocentre
supports: 150 scripts analysed: consumer-credit terms averaged 24 words and can add 10+ seconds; radioGauge database of 550+ campaigns (239 with terms): long terms had little effect on ad awareness but lower involvement, identity and impression scores, and attention fell in the last 5 seconds

title: 7 Ways to Create Billboards that Spark Joy (27 February 2019)
publisher: OAAA (Out of Home Advertising Association of America)
supports: Bold sans serif type, strong contrast, one message, seven words or fewer, localisation, strong silhouette; a message not understood in a few seconds is lost

title: Digital billboards issue brief
supports: Digital billboards show static messages that rotate typically every six or eight seconds, with no flashing, scrolling or full motion; brightness rules

title: The ABX Guide to Out-of-Home Advertising Creative Effectiveness (Mid-Year 2024)
publisher: Advertising Benchmark Index (ABX), hosted by OAAA
supports: Seven best practices from testing 16,000 OOH ads; named high and low scorers against an ABX norm of 100, including Amazon Prime (135), Comfort (126), Qantas credit card (72), AMEX (47) and CMC Markets (40)

title: About responsive search ads
supports: Up to 15 headlines of 30 characters and 4 descriptions of 90; paths of 15; pinning trade-offs; at least two RSAs per ad group; Google's internal figures on Ad Strength and extra RSAs (August 2025 data)

title: Editorial (Google Ads policy)
supports: No gimmicky capitalisation, punctuation, symbols, repetition or spacing; no phone numbers in ad text; the business must be identified; accepted spelling and grammar; warning at least 7 days before suspension

title: Facebook Feed image ad specs (Meta Ads Guide)
supports: Primary text 50 to 150 characters and headline 27 characters recommended for Feed; 4:5 at 1440 x 1800

title: Book description (Kindle Direct Publishing help)
supports: 4,000-character limit including HTML; allowed formatting; no reviews, quotes or testimonials, contact details, time-sensitive information, prices, spoilers, emojis or keyword lists in the description

title: Every Door Direct Mail
supports: Mail to every address on chosen carrier routes, addressed to Postal Customer; Census filters; Retail EDDM minimum 200 pieces and maximum 5,000 per day per ZIP Code; indicia rules

title: Mailing Preference Service
publisher: MPS, run with the Data & Marketing Association (UK)
supports: Free UK register to opt out of unsolicited addressed marketing mail; licensees screen their lists against it; registration can take up to three months; it does not cover unaddressed mail or mail to 'The Occupier'
